digest_title: Daily Security Digest: Verifying Dependencies and Ecosystem Alerts
dek: ShadowContext analyzes verification strategies for Cowlib memory exhaustion vulnerabilities and expanded malicious package alerts.
overview: Defenders must verify dependency trees for CVE-2026-59248 in Cowlib and ensure proper alert routing for expanded open source malware feeds.

stories.headline: Cowlib Memory Exhaustion Flaw Requires Dependency-Level Proof
stories.summary: CVE-2026-59248 causes excessive memory usage during HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 header decoding, requiring careful verification of resolved versions in dependency graphs.
stories.why_it_matters: Top-level release checks are insufficient because hidden transitive dependencies can leave services exposed to denial-of-service risks.

stories.headline: OpenSSF Malware Ingestion Expands GitHub Dependabot Alert Coverage
stories.summary: GitHub now ingests OpenSSF malicious-package reports beyond npm, improving ecosystem coverage for supply chain threats like typosquatting and malicious binaries.
stories.why_it_matters: Enabling alerts is only the first step; teams must verify ecosystem coverage, notification routing, and dependency graph accuracy.

operating_view: Maintain rigorous visibility into transitive dependencies and ensure alert feeds map directly to active operational ownership and remediation workflows.
watch_items: Confirm actual Cowlib library versions in locked build artifacts.
Verify active repository subscription settings for expanded Dependabot feeds.
Map protocol reachability for internet-facing Erlang and Elixir services.
